newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's security tsar sees danger of army mutiny.
newsitem.headline: Russia's security tsar sees danger of army mutiny.

text.p: Russia's security supremo Alexander Lebed said in an interview published on Wednesday that the armed forces, driven to the limit by government negligence and unpaid wages, may go on the rampage soon.
"An armed mutiny may take place this autumn," Lebed told Vechernyaya Moskva daily newspaper. The outspoken and publicity-seeking general has a record of making controversial remarks.

Lebed accused the government of underestimating tension in the armed forces and called the situation a "national disgrace". He drew a historical parallel with the tsarist Russian army which, exhausted and demoralised in World War One, was unable to resist the Bolshevik uprising.
"People with high professional skills serve in the army. Maybe it is not enough to win world wars but it is definitely enough to slaughter all the lambs," Lebed said.

Lebed, who does not hide his presidential ambitions despite being a senior member of the team around the ailing President Boris Yeltsin, said he could salvage the situation in the country but did not have enough power.
"I have a plan but do not have powers to implement it because those are the powers of the head of state," he said.
